blocks.explanation:
A sum of three sines of different angles equal to zero.
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Plan: pair \(\sin 7x\) with \(\sin 3x\) (their angles average to \(5x\)), use \(\sin C + \sin D\), take out \(\sin 5x\), and solve each factor.
steps:
Given: \(\sin 3x - \sin 5x + \sin 7x = 0\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Method: \(\sin C + \sin D = 2\sin\frac{C+D}{2}\cos\frac{C-D}{2}\). Pairing \(7x\) with \(3x\) gives \(\sin 5x\), the same as the middle term, so a common factor appears.

Join \(\sin 7x\) and \(\sin 3x\)
\[\sin 7x + \sin 3x\]
\[= 2\sin\tfrac{7x + 3x}{2}\cos\tfrac{7x - 3x}{2}\]
\[= 2\sin 5x\cos 2x\]
Why: sum-to-product formula with \(C = 7x\), \(D = 3x\).

Factorise
\[2\sin 5x\cos 2x - \sin 5x = 0\]
\[\sin 5x(2\cos 2x - 1) = 0\]
\[\sin 5x = 0 \text{ or } \cos 2x = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: \(\sin 5x\) is common; a product is zero only when a factor is zero.

When \(\sin 5x = 0\)
\[5x = n\pi \;\Rightarrow\; x = \tfrac{n\pi}{5}\]
In \([0, 2\pi]\) (\(n = 0, \ldots, 10\)):
\[0, \tfrac{\pi}{5}, \tfrac{2\pi}{5}, \tfrac{3\pi}{5}, \tfrac{4\pi}{5}, \pi,\]
\[\tfrac{6\pi}{5}, \tfrac{7\pi}{5}, \tfrac{8\pi}{5}, \tfrac{9\pi}{5}, 2\pi\]
Why: sine is zero at every multiple of \(\pi\).

When \(\cos 2x = \frac{1}{2}\)
\[2x = \tfrac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi \text{ or } \tfrac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\]
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{6} + n\pi \text{ or } \tfrac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi\]
In \([0, 2\pi]\): \(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{11\pi}{6}\).
Why: cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), period \(2\pi\); divide by 2.

Collect the answers
\[\left\{\tfrac{n\pi}{5}\right\} \cup \left\{\tfrac{\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\tfrac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\}\]
Why: no value of one family equals a value of another (\(\frac{\pi}{6}\) is not a multiple of \(\frac{\pi}{5}\)), so in \([0, 2\pi]\) there are \(11 + 4 = 15\) values.
blocks.final_answer:
In \([0, 2\pi]\) (15 values): \(x = 0, \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{5}, \frac{2\pi}{5}, \frac{3\pi}{5}, \frac{4\pi}{5}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \pi, \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{6\pi}{5}, \frac{7\pi}{5}, \frac{8\pi}{5}, \frac{9\pi}{5}, \frac{11\pi}{6}, 2\pi\)
General solution \(= \left\{\frac{n\pi}{5}\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\)
